page: Microsoft Azure L48ps_v5 is an arm64-based virtual machine within Azure's storage-optimized Lpsv5 family. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and provides 48 dedicated ARM processor virtual cores paired with 384 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

A defining hardware characteristic of this configuration is its 11,520 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. This integrated local NVMe capacity provides massive local disk space designed for high sustained IOPS and low-latency disk operations without relying on network-attached storage disks. The VM operates without GPU acceleration hardware, focusing its system architecture entirely on dense general compute, memory allocation, and high-throughput local storage access.

Utilizing the ARM64 architecture delivers compute efficiency for workloads built and compiled for 64-bit ARM environments. Tradeoffs include the non-persistent, ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe disks upon VM deallocation, as well as the requirement for software compatibility with ARM binaries. The hardware profile fits I/O-intensive workloads such as distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, data warehousing, high-throughput caching tiers, and large-scale log analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure L48ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated ARM64 processor cores and 384 GB of system memory on Microsoft Hyper-V. Delivering an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation, the instance is equipped with 11,520 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, eliminating network disk latency for data-intensive operations. The instance lacks specialized GPU acceleration, directing its hardware profile toward high-throughput data processing and dense local capacity. Operating on the ARM instruction set, the configuration provides operational efficiency for software natively compiled for arm64 targets. Tradeoffs include the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe disks and the prerequisite for ARM software ecosystem compatibility. This hardware profile suits large transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics platforms, large caching layers, and search index workloads demanding low-latency I/O alongside substantial memory.
